_what: The Interface Standard: numeric, sourced rules a screen must meet, measured from what renders by engine/measure.ts. Product-independent. Each rule names its sources (fetched 2026-11-10) and whether the number is a hard floor (WCAG 2.2 AA) or a house value chosen above the floor, with the reason. A product may make a rule stricter in its profile; it may never loosen one. A rule changes only on the governor's word, recorded in ESCAPES.md.

root.says: A top-level place reached from the main navigation (home, search, saved, the maker's studio home). No Back.

flow-step.says: One step of a sequence (joining, sign-in, reset, confirmation). Back to the previous step or the door it came from.

sub-screen.says: A screen reached from inside another (a work, a maker, About, a settings page). Back.

editor.says: A screen that edits one thing (a work, a profile). Cancel or Back, and one primary action.

dialog.says: A sheet or dialog over another screen. Close.

operator.says: An internal operator screen. Same measures; Back to the queue.

rules.says: Reading text (paragraphs, list items) is at least 16 px on a phone.
source: Material 3 Body Large 16sp — androidx material3 tokens/TypeScaleTokens.kt
GOV.UK body 19px on all screens — https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/type-scale/
rules.status: house (above M3 floor; GOV.UK is stricter)

rules.says: A form label is at least 16 px — as large as what is typed into the field.
source: GOV.UK labels and inputs at 19px — govuk-frontend 6.6.0 label and input mixins
Material 3 Label Large 14sp is the floor — TypeScaleTokens.kt
governor 2026-11-10: 'Fonts too small' on Join step 2 (labels measured 13 px)

rules.says: Help text, captions and secondary lines are at least 14 px (short uppercase tracked labels — tab names, status words, step counters — are held to the 12 px floor instead).
source: Material 3 Body Medium 14sp — TypeScaleTokens.kt
Material 3 Label Medium 12sp for short labels and navigation-bar labels — TypeScaleTokens.kt
governor 2026-11-10: 'Fonts too small' (help 14 px kept as the floor, labels raised)

rules.says: No text anywhere is under 12 px — eyebrows, tab names and metadata included.
source: Material 3 Body Small / Label Medium 12sp — TypeScaleTokens.kt
the product's own foundation: 'No text is set below 12 px' (ux/INTERFACE_FOUNDATION.md)
rules.status: house (Apple's 11pt minimum is lower; 12 is the stricter of the two)

rules.says: Running text has a line height of at least 1.4.
source: Material 3 body 24/16 = 1.5, 20/14 = 1.43 — TypeScaleTokens.kt
WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing 1.5 must not break — https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing.html

rules.says: A line of running text is at most 80 characters.
source: WCAG 1.4.8 'no more than 80 characters' — https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#visual-presentation
Baymard 50–75 optimal — https://baymard.com/blog/line-length-readability
rules.status: AAA criterion adopted as house rule

rules.says: Every control is at least 44 × 44 px, except a link inside a sentence.
source: WCAG 2.5.5 44×44 (AAA) — https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced.html
Material 48×48dp — https://m3.material.io/foundations/designing/structure
Apple 44×44pt — https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility
WCAG 2.5.8 24×24 is the hard floor (AA)
rules.status: house (AAA; the product foundation already sets 44)

rules.says: Every screen that is not a top-level place shows Back (or Close / Cancel) in the top bar, at every width.
source: Android: Up shows on every destination except the start destination — https://developer.android.com/guide/navigation/principles
GOV.UK: 'Always include a Back link component at the top of question pages' — https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/question-pages/
Apple: 'Use the standard Back and Close buttons.' — HIG navigation bars
governor 2026-11-10: 'How does one go back from this page?' (Join step 2)
rules.status: house (synthesis of platform rules; fail-closed by archetype, never by route list)

rules.says: At most one primary action is visible on a screen.
source: Material 3 buttons: one high-emphasis action per screen region — https://m3.material.io/components/all-buttons
the product's drawing board (one docked action)

rules.says: Forms breathe: label 4 px or more above its input, inputs at least 48 px tall, help text 4 px or more below its input, and 32 px or more between one field and the next.
source: GOV.UK form group 20px (small) / 30px (large); label gap 5px — govuk-frontend 6.6.0 _form-group, label mixins
Material 3 text field min height 56dp, supporting text 4dp below — TextFieldDefaults.kt, TextFieldImpl.kt
governor 2026-11-10: 'Items too cramped together' (fields measured 24 px apart with 13 px labels)
rules.status: house (field gap above GOV.UK's small-screen 20 px, at its large-screen value rounded to the 4 px grid)

rules.says: On a phone, text keeps at least 16 px from the screen edge.
source: Material 3 compact window margins 16dp — https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/breakpoints/compact (partly verified)
GOV.UK 15px — govuk-frontend width container

rules.says: Nothing scrolls sideways, down to 320 px wide.
source: WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA) — https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#reflow

rules.says: Spacing sits on the product's declared base unit (4 px).
source: the product's foundation: 4 px base unit, 8/16/24/32/48 rhythm (ux/INTERFACE_FOUNDATION.md)
Material 3 spacing tokens on a 4/8dp scale (UNVERIFIED: page not fetched)

rules.says: No axe violation under WCAG 2.2 A and AA, with target-size and colour contrast switched on.
source: WCAG 1.4.3 contrast 4.5:1 — https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum
axe target-size is disabled by default; enabled by the wcag22aa tag — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dequelabs/axe-core/develop/lib/rules/target-size.json

manual.says: The screen is set beside two named reference apps of its archetype at the same width, and the comparison is shown to the governor as one image.
manual.why_manual: taste and character cannot be measured

manual.says: The first thing the eye lands on is the screen's purpose; the primary action is obvious.
manual.why_manual: attention order is a human judgement; the engine bounds it with IS-A1 and the type floors
